rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words — grep zero-tolerance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm the rule prevents: consultancy/lab register that flinches an engineer reader mid-instruction. Present here. L5: 'This is crucially the step that changes how the run behaves.' Ran on the body region only: sed -n '1,65p' <file> | grep -nE '\b(crucial|crucially|honest|delve|importantly|substrate|synergize|paradigm shift)\b' -> one hit, line 5. Em-dash half of the same rule is clean: same body slice, grep -c '—' -> 0, with the pattern proved live by grep -c '—' over the whole file -> 17 (all in the maintainer region).
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Drop the adverb; the sentence is filler with or without it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Ritual / ceremony — hard ban
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: SAFe/ceremony register in a training whose whole argument is that the loop replaces the ceremony. Present. L11: 'Treat this as a ritual you repeat at the start of every session.' Command: sed -n '1,65p' <file> | grep -nE '\b(ritual|ceremony)\b' -> 11:Treat this as a ritual... The AE101 practice(n) carve-out does not reach 'ritual', which is banned absolutely.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Word is 'exercise' or 'move'; or cut the line, which claims a per-session repetition nothing in the arc asks for.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: changelog in a file a student reads; rules are rules, history is git. Present, and in the body region (line 49 < maintainer cut at 66), not in a maintainer provenance header where the corpus convention would protect it. L49: 'This section previously said something different; it was fixed on 2026-01-14.' Transition verbs quoted as the rule demands: 'previously said', 'was fixed'. Command: sed -n '1,65p' <file> | grep -nE '20[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}' -> 49 only.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Delete the sentence outright; nothing forward-binding is in it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Credit original when paraphrasing named technique.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest lines: L3 '**Time:** 20 minutes.' sits exactly at line 3 directly under the H1, single total, no phase breakdown or slot context, which is what the timing-location clause asks of an atomic exercise. Creator-name half: sed -n '1,65p' <file> | grep -nE '\b(Antti|the creator|the author|training creator)\b' -> no output (pattern proved on the maintainer region, where 'Antti' appears at L72). Author-we half: no first-person-plural body sentence; the only 'we' forms sit inside prompt fences ('the bug we just fixed'), which the rule keeps.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Always "you", never "the student"; teacher framing stays out of body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: third-person teacher voice leaking into the page the student reads, so the reader is described rather than addressed. Present twice over in one line. L24: 'At this point the student should notice the test is still red.' Command: sed -n '1,65p' <file> | grep -n 'the student' -> 24. It is also delivery mechanics ('at this point... should notice'), which the same rule routes below the maintainer cut. Neither the Connections room-harvest carve-out nor the maintainer-block exception reaches line 24.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Either address the reader directly or move the beat below the fence; note it also asserts a red test in an exercise that runs after the fix shipped.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Over-hedge detector.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: reassurance tells a senior reader the author thought the beat needed defending. Present. L37: 'There is no penalty if you skip this, and it is completely fine either way.' 'no penalty' is a named flag phrase in the rule; the second clause repeats the first. It also sits between the prompt and the push-back line that carries the real instruction, so cutting it costs nothing.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut the sentence; L39's push-back line already carries the beat.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Punchy framing keeps punch; carve-out lives downstream.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a slogan with no boundary paragraph is read at full width. Present, and the file itself is the witness. L57 states the slogan bare: 'Anything can be inspected and reverse-engineered with an LLM: a codebase nobody documented, a CI pipeline, a config, an API you did not write...'. The backing block's stance at L134 says the boundary 'lives in the third bullet per check_writing.md §12' and instructs judges to 'read the third bullet before flagging'. The section has two bullets: sed -n '55,59p' <file> shows L57 and L58 and nothing else. The carve-out the keep-note relies on is not in the body, so the slogan stands uncarved and the keep-note is stale against its passage.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Restore one Boris-direct boundary bullet (extraction quality tracks the quality of what was sampled), or rewrite the stance note to match what the body now carries.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The `**What happened:**` block is OPTIONAL — default is to omit it
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest call in the file. L60-64 carries the recap. It clears the three moves: count plus noun ('Two things came out of one ticket'), one qualifier on what makes it the student's ('the conventions your team has been encoding in its fields all along'), and it lands on a destination rather than a pat ('The field rules stay in the scrollback. The next exercise sweeps this whole session.'). Past tense throughout, per the same rule's tense clause. 43 words, slightly over the 25-40 band, which is the only thing that came near.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest line is L5, 'This is crucially the step that changes how the run behaves.' — a deictic opener of the shape the rule's (b) clause names. It stays inside because the clause states its own claim rather than pointing at a claim made elsewhere, so deleting the pointer would not leave a standing sentence. The line is flagged under check_writing §1 and check_student_facing §33 instead, which is where its actual defects live.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slogan that is false as stated is not punchy framing — run the truth test before reaching for §12.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L57's 'Anything can be inspected and reverse-engineered with an LLM'. The superlative tell fires, but the backing block at L133-135 records this as a maintainer-attested L1 stance held deliberately, with the reach of 'anything' listed as the contested edge and a named fallback if it fails. Per the preamble, a rule question rather than a REVISE: the claim has true readings across the artifacts it names, so §12's remedy is the right one and the defect is the missing carve-out, filed on §12.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A sentence saying how you'd know points at the outcome, not the nearest artifact.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L53, 'Does it sound like the comments already on the ticket?' This is the how-you-would-know clause for the register beat, and it points at an artifact outside the agent's own output (comments written by the team before this session), so it can come back negative. Had it read 'does Claude think it sounds right', it would be the self-witnessing shape the rule exists to catch.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L43 'Adding a connector is one command per tracker.' — 'connector' arrives cold. It stays inside on two grounds the rule states: the assumed-known carve-out tracks the AE101 engineer audience, and the file's maintainer block carries an explicit accept-note at L72 ('"Connector" is assumed-known vocabulary (Antti 2026-08-18) ... findings on it are overruled — do not re-file'). Checked the accept-notes before scoring, as the carve-out instructs.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Golden path only in body — THIS RULE HAS AN EXCEPTION; read to the boundary before cutting anything.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L18 'If there is no ticket for this bug, say so in the chat' and L30 'No ticket of your own to read? Any other real ticket from your tracker works.' Both are branch-shaped, and both clear the base test: the failure is plausible in a real tracker, the rescue is one non-obvious line, and routing either below the fence would delete it from every surface a student or trainer sees.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The register beat at L53 is the passage this rule's own precedent clause names, so both halves were run rather than one. Exempt clause: reading for register is allowed where error-catching is not. Other clauses re-run and clear: the object is named ('the comments already on the ticket'), the tell is named ('if the wording feels off'), the speech verb carries its addressee ('tell Claude which line and how you'd write it'). Nearest miss is 'off or wrong', a doubled adjective, not a rule breach.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No em-dashes. Simple sentences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: sed -n '1,65p' <file> | grep -c '—' -> 0. Pattern proved live: grep -c '—' over the whole file -> 17, all of them below the maintainer cut at line 66. Sentences in the body run short and single-clause.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Section headers use command verbs when section is about doing something.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Four of five section headers lead with a verb: 'Read the ticket for your bug', 'Read the conventions off the ticket', 'Write the close-out and send it', 'Double-check the voice'. Closest miss is L55 '## Anything can be reverse-engineered', declarative over a section whose second bullet is an instruction. It stays as authored: the backing stance at L134 records the bare statement as the deliberate slogan placement, and renaming it to a verb would delete the frame the section exists to land.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Inline links use target's title, never filename.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L43 links as '[MCP and connectors](../trainings/agentic-engineering-101/reference/mcp-and-connectors.md)'. Link text is the target's title, not a filename and not a backticked path, which is what this rule governs. The '../' path form is explicitly out of this rule's scope per its own boundary clause, which records a prior judge filing a TODO on exactly that; not re-filed here. Ordinals clause also clean: no 'Step N' or 'Phase N' cross-references in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: LLM-vs-agent-vs-Claude vocabulary discipline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The split is held deliberately across the body: acting goes to 'the agent' (L18 'The agent will offer to create one', L29 'The agent separates strong signals from guesses'), invocation goes to 'Claude' (L33, L45, L53 'Ask Claude to...'), and the one capability-about-thinking sentence keeps 'LLM' (L57 'reverse-engineered with an LLM'). Counts are balanced, not the 10:0 Claude-heavy shape the audit signal names.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Session / task / run split (all trainings).
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: noun-'run' for the agent's sitting collides with the word the training reserves for test/CI/eval executions, so the student loses the one-session-one-task frame. Present. L5: 'This is crucially the step that changes how the run behaves.' Command: sed -n '1,65p' <file> | grep -n 'the run' -> 5. Not one of the survivals the rule allows: no test/CI/eval execution, no quote, no path or branch name, not the 'long-running' adjective. The file uses 'session' correctly everywhere else (L11, L43, L64).
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: 'the session' if the sitting is meant, or cut the sentence with the §1 fix.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cut NVA: true but not moving student forward.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L43's tail, 'and it pays back on every session after this one' — a rationale clause rather than a move. It survives on the value question: it is the only thing telling the student why to spend a command now rather than paste fields forever, and the maintainer block at L74 records the one-pointer shape as deliberate. Nearest genuine NVA in the file, L37, is filed under check_writing §9.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body "read it" / "look at it" / "notice X" after chat-print = dead weight.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L53 after the close-out prompt prints what it wrote. It clears the carve-out because it names the specific thing under inspection and the decision that follows ('Does it sound like the comments already on the ticket? ... tell Claude which line and how you'd write it'), rather than the banned bare 'read it'. L24, 'the student should notice', is narration of a read, but its defect is third-person teacher voice and it is filed under check_writing §7.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself — subject test, then deletion test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: the training describing its own shape to a student who came for the work. Present at L5: 'This is crucially the step that changes how the run behaves.' Subject test: the sentence is about a step of this exercise, not the student's ticket, agent or artifact, so it is arc-positioning. Deletion test: cut it and L3's Time line joins L7's 'What you do:' cleanly, losing nothing. Not covered by the signposting exemption, which lists '**The point:**' (present separately at L13) and the canonical sections, not a free-standing line above them.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Delete the line; '**The point:**' at L13 already carries what it was reaching for.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No placeholders inside fences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -nE '\[[A-Za-z ]+\]' over the expanded view returns one hit, line 61, and it is the markdown link text on L43 of the source, not fence content (pattern proved live: printf 'x [BRACKET] y' | grep -c -> 1). The first prompt uses the open-hook shape the rule prefers: internal action paragraph, then a bare 'Ticket:' line last, with the body lead-in at L20 naming the slot.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every prompt block: one-sentence action lead-in.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All three markers carry a command-verb lead-in under 20 words: L20 'Drop the ticket link after the colon.', L33 'Ask Claude to reverse-engineer how your team handles bugs and propose five bug rules.', L45 'Ask Claude to write the close-out, update the ticket, and report what it wrote.' L20 is the dangling-colon sub-case done the way 2a prescribes: the input instruction alone, no summary of a fence about to be read.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Tell me what you wrote, not show me what you'll write.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The side-effecting prompt (close-the-ticket-3, expanded view L68) ends 'Tell me what you wrote.' rather than pre-confirming, and the body lead-in at L45 mirrors it ('report what it wrote'). A tracker comment is reversible, so the irreversible-action carve-out does not apply and the post-action report is the right default.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body lead-in mirrors prompt's opening phrasing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest pair is the second: body L33 'Ask Claude to reverse-engineer how your team handles bugs...' against the fence opening 'Reverse-engineer how this team handles bugs from one bug ticket.' Same verb, same noun phrase. The third pair rhymes on 'update the ticket'. First pair is the deliberate open-hook exception rather than drift.

findings.quote: This is crucially the step that changes how the run behaves.
findings.harm: Banned word 'crucially' in body prose; lab/consultancy register mid-instruction.
findings.fix: Cut the line, or drop the adverb.

findings.quote: Treat this as a ritual you repeat at the start of every session.
findings.harm: Hard-banned 'ritual' on a curriculum surface; imports the ceremony register the loop is meant to replace.
findings.fix: Use 'exercise' or 'move', or cut the sentence, which asserts a per-session repetition nothing else in the arc asks for.

findings.quote: This section previously said something different; it was fixed on 2026-01-14.
findings.harm: Session biography in body prose: 'previously said' and 'was fixed' are transition verbs, and the reader loses nothing if the clause vanishes.
findings.fix: Delete the sentence. History is git.

findings.quote: At this point the student should notice the test is still red.
findings.harm: Third-person teacher voice plus delivery mechanics in body; the reader is described rather than addressed.
findings.fix: Address the reader in second person or route the beat below the maintainer fence.

todos.note: 'There is no penalty if you skip this, and it is completely fine either way.' — 'no penalty' is a named over-hedge flag and the second clause repeats the first. Cut; L39 carries the beat.

'Anything can be inspected and reverse-engineered with an LLM' stands with no boundary paragraph. The backing stance at L134 tells judges to read 'the third bullet' before flagging, but the section has only two bullets (L57, L58). Restore the carve-out bullet or correct the stale keep-note.
'changes how the run behaves' — noun-'run' for the agent's sitting is banned in student-facing body; 'session' is the word, and the file uses it correctly at L11, L43 and L64.

'This is crucially the step that changes how the run behaves.' — the exercise narrating its own place in the arc. Deletion test passes cleanly: L3 joins L7 with nothing lost, and '**The point:**' at L13 already does this job.

notes: Reported per the dispatch instruction for this bench fire: rows only for rules that actually had something to say (REVISE, or a PASS that came close), not a full N/A ledger. Every writing-class rule in the derived brief was read in full first: derive-class-brief.js assembled 129 rules across check_writing.md (26), check_student_facing.md (35), check_prompts.md (48), check_sales_copy.md (13) and check_strategy_tie_in.md (7), kept=129 dropped=0, and the brief reported 'all compendiums read' with no prefill. check_sales_copy.md and check_strategy_tie_in.md produced no rows: the file is an AE101 exercise body, not buyer-facing copy, and it carries no Big Idea / Key Concepts / What You'll Learn section for the strategy rules to bind to. Body view: maintainer_cut=66, fence_ranges=[] (prompts arrive as {{prompt:...}} markers; the expanded view at curriculum/evals/body-views/shared--file--writing-5plant.expanded.md was used for the prompt-class rules), body region = lines 1-65. Every cited line was re-read in the raw source before filing. Out-of-lane observations, not scored: (a) L24 asserts the test is still red, while the file's own maintainer block at L70 places this exercise after fix-tests-first with the PR already shipped, which is a technical/pedagogy contradiction rather than a writing one; (b) the missing third bullet under 'Anything can be reverse-engineered' also leaves the backing block's stance at L134 describing a body that does not exist, which a backing-validation run would catch.
